description.fun: Hoppip is so light that a breeze lifts it off the ground, so when it senses strong winds coming it links leaves with other Hoppip or grips the ground with its feet. Drifting on the wind has spread it all over the world, except the cold places. Its family's English names spell out 'hop, skip and jump', one stage at a time.
description.guide: A small, pink plant Pokémon of the Grass and Flying types, so light that the wind carries it long distances. It links leaves with other Hoppip to avoid being blown away by strong winds. It evolves into Skiploom and then Jumpluff.
description.tagline: Light enough to blow away, and happy to let it happen

description.fun: Skiploom works as a living thermometer: the flower on its head opens once it's warmer than 18 °C and closes again when it cools. It floats up to get closer to the sun, ducks under a tree when it rains, and flies off to warmer places when the weather turns cold. Some people claim they can tell where a Skiploom was born from the scent of its flower.
description.guide: The middle stage of the Hoppip line, a Grass and Flying-type plant Pokémon with a flower on its head. The flower opens and closes with the temperature, so it is sometimes used as a thermometer. It migrates to warmer places when it gets cold.
description.tagline: A floating flower that blooms above 18 °C

description.fun: Jumpluff rides seasonal winds around the globe, steering with its three cotton puffs so skilfully that it stays in control even in a hurricane. It scatters cotton spores as it travels to make new Jumpluff, and breathing them in makes you itch and cough. When its spores run out, its journey ends, and so does its life.
description.guide: The final form of Hoppip, a Grass and Flying-type Pokémon with three large cotton puffs. It drifts on seasonal winds across the world, scattering cotton spores to reproduce. At 3 kg it is the lightest Pokémon to have evolved twice.
description.tagline: Drifts the world on cotton puffs until the spores run out
